cold_precondition.definition_used: FlashBoot off; pending_jobs = 0; initializing = 0; running = 0; all endpoint pods EXITED / uptime 0 (GraphQL). A logical RunPod standby slot (idle/throttled) is not by itself a live worker/container.
cold_precondition.original_definition: sum of ALL /health worker states == 0 (including idle/throttled standby slots).
cold_precondition.why_changed: RunPod keeps one standby slot assigned to the endpoint (workersStandby=1) even with zero traffic; /health reports it as idle ('scaled down, waiting for requests', pod desiredStatus=EXITED, uptime 0) or throttled (host GPU busy). The all-states-zero condition is only met transiently while RunPod is between hosts, so attempt 1 with the original precondition spent the full 900 s preflight timeout on run 1 without ever submitting a job.
cold_precondition.script_change: scripts/pilot/infra_10/_common.sh: workers_total -> workers_alive (initializing+running) + pods_alive (GraphQL EXITED check); wait_zero_workers requires both plus empty queue.

cold_precondition.what_is_measured: container start on an assigned RTX 5090 host + network volume mount + handler start (torch import, CUDA context) + weight/path validation + RunPod scheduling. Image pull onto the host is NOT included when the slot is idle; it IS included when RunPod must (re)initialize the worker (run 1 started from a throttled slot: throttled -> initializing -> idle -> running).

runpod_timings_note: delayTime = provider-reported pre-execution delay (not to be called GPU queue time as a whole); executionTime = readiness handler execution (0.28-0.35 s in all runs). Kept separately; never subtracted from the formal start-to-READY metric.
